newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL to invest HUF 49 bln in Duna refinery.
newsitem.headline: MOL to invest HUF 49 bln in Duna refinery.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt will spend a total 49 billion forints on a residue upgrading project and a hydrogen plant at its Duna refinery, the company said on Thursday.
"These two projects will help to increase the company's profitability and to increase the share of the high value, environmentally friendly products," MOL said in a statement.
The residue upgrading project worth 43 billion forints is due to start at the beginning of 1998 and is expected to be completed by the end of the year 2000, the statement added.
As a result of the investment, MOL will be able to convert its heavy fuel oil into high value products, mainly gasoline and gasoils, the company said.

The other project, the construction of a six billion forints hydrogen plant at the Duna refinery, will start at the beginning of 1999 and is expected to be completed by the midlle of the year 2000, MOL said.

"The implementation of the hydrogen plant is driven by the residue upgrading project and the higher hydrogen usage of the prduction and a result of stricter Hungarian product specification," MOL said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, MOL shares rallied to a new record high of 4,350 forints on Wednesday before retreating to close at 4,335 forints, up 245.
